content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "This judge text resolves a collision between the challenger's and defender's chains by comparing their footing and support.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "The phrase weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse can mean noting missing explicit naming as part of support or forbidding any word-for-word naming test; I read it as forbidding the judge to discount a footed chain for not explicitly naming Joseph.", "why": "It discounts the challenger's footed chain because it does not explicitly name Joseph, which is a word-for-word stating test rather than chain-against-chain footing."}
